text:
If your Tuesday plans can wait for the afternoon, the damp gray start should ease, though Burlington likely stays mostly cloudy and cool. Showers are clearing this morning, but lingering low-level moisture will keep the sky stubborn, with a high right around 61 and a north wind around 6 to 9 mph. On the lake, north winds start at 15 to 20 knots before easing, with waves up to 2 feet, so this is a better day for a shoreline walk than a small-boat outing. The water is 62 and the level is normal.

Tonight stays mostly cloudy with a low near 49, then Wednesday brings the payoff: partly sunny skies, light winds, and a high around 71. Dense fog is possible early, including near the lake, but it should turn into a much friendlier afternoon. Keep longer waterfront plans for Wednesday, and if you're heading out today, wait until after the morning showers and avoid the broad lake until the wind settles.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Tuesday! Our Tuesday starts off with some low clouds, fog and morning mist. It looks like we should be able to slowly clear away the low-level clouds, fog and mist into this afternoon. But even still, higher level clouds remain fairly stubborn. Portions of northern New York may be able to break apart some clouds and get some sunshine going just before sunset this evening. Daytime highs are generally in the 50s to lower 60s come this afternoon. Lows tonight fall back into the 40s and lower 50s to start Wednesday.
